transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um… I’m here because I keep not finishing things all the way at work. Like I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I miss the last parts. Even though I know it really matters and my job depends on getting it right.
Do you find it hard to stay focused or do you get distracted easily when you're trying to finish tasks at work?

Yeah… I do. I’ll start the shift really trying to stay focused, but after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels kind of all run together. Then I’ll realize I’m just staring at the same tray or the log sheet and not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next.
Do you have similar problems with finishing tasks or staying focused when you're not at work, like at home or in your personal life?
I’m not really sure. I mean… at home I don’t track it the same way. I guess I don’t notice it as much unless something doesn’t get done, but… I don’t know.
Can you think of any examples at home or in your personal life where you’ve started something but didn’t finish it, even though you knew it was important?

Um… I can’t think of a clear home example right now. The main thing I know is at work — I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, and then somehow I leave off the last parts, even though I know I’m supposed to finish them exactly.
Can you think of any times outside of work, like when you’re cooking, reading, or doing something you enjoy, where you’ve started something but didn’t finish it even though you meant to?

I can’t really think of something like cooking or reading right now. It’s more… the work stuff that keeps happening. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and then I somehow miss the last parts, even though I know it has to be done right.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever started doing something simple, like brushing your teeth, sending an email, or making a phone call, but then didn’t finish it even though you meant to?

Not really with things like brushing my teeth or phone calls… at least I can’t think of one. It’s more the work stuff I mentioned. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, and then somehow the last parts don’t get done, even though I know they have to be.
Can you tell me if you sometimes have trouble starting tasks, even when you know they need to be done — like starting a project at work or even something small like filling out a form?

Yeah… mostly with the certification modules, or long procedure readings. I know I need to do them, but I put them off until the last possible minute. Sitting there trying to take in all the rules just feels… really draining.
Can you tell me if you sometimes have trouble finishing routine things, like housework, chores, or even small daily tasks, even though you know they need to be done?

I guess… not so much housework that comes to mind. It’s more at work. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and then somehow I leave out the last parts. Even though I know it has to be finished right.

Can you think of any times when you’ve been reading something that required focus, like instructions or a detailed article, where you started but didn’t finish because it felt too hard to stay with it?

Yeah… the certification modules, mostly. Or long procedure readings. I’ll start them, but I usually put them off until I absolutely have to because trying to sit there and take in all the rules feels… exhausting, honestly.

Can you tell me if you have similar trouble focusing or finishing things when you’re reading for pleasure, watching something that requires attention, or doing a task that you find mentally challenging but not work-related?

Yeah… I mean, I notice it more with things that feel demanding. Even if I start my shift trying to really focus, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels sort of blur together. I’ll catch myself just staring at the same tray or log sheet and not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next.
Can you think of any times when you’ve had trouble finishing basic daily routines, like getting dressed, making a simple meal, or tidying up, even though you knew you needed to complete them?

Not really those things, I guess. It’s more… what I was saying with work. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, and then I somehow don’t finish the last parts, even though I know it has to be done right.
Can you think of any times when you’ve started something like folding laundry, organizing a drawer, or following a recipe, and then just stopped midway even though you knew you needed to finish it?

Not so much drawers or recipes… but the same kind of thing happens at work. I’ll start sanitation steps or the batch logs, and then somehow the last parts just don’t get done, even though I know they have to be right. It’s… kind of the main reason I’m here.

Can you tell me if you’ve noticed these same kinds of problems — starting tasks but not finishing them, or having trouble staying focused — in any other parts of your life, like school, social situations, or managing personal responsibilities?

Yeah… school, mostly. My mom still has some of my old report cards from elementary school, like around fourth grade, and they’d say I was bright but needed a lot of reminders to finish classwork or turn in homework. I do remember understanding the material, but if the teacher wasn’t kind of right there, I’d miss parts of the instructions or not finish things.

latest_inference.note: The patient reported a history of difficulty finishing tasks in school (elementary school report cards indicating problems with completing classwork and homework despite understanding material), along with consistent difficulties in task completion and focus at work involving structured processes. This supports a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation (F90.0). Other candidates (F48.1, F06.81, F32.9) were ruled out due to lack of evidence supporting anxiety, mood, or psychotic disorders.
